chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, raising it, said:

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to Isa, son of Maryam (peace be upon him): 'O Isa! Let your tongue in the secret and the public be one tongue, and similarly your heart. Indeed, I warn you of yourself, and suffice with Me as an All-Knowing.'
Two tongues are not suitable in one mouth, nor two swords in one sheath, and similarly are the minds.

key_terms.أُحَذِّرُكَ نَفْسَكَ: I warn you of yourself (guarding against the self's deceit)

ai.seo_question: What does the concept of 'two tongues in one mouth' signify in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith qudsi where God addresses Isa (peace be upon him), warning against the spiritual danger of the self (nafs) through the metaphor of 'two tongues' to illustrate the incompatibility of inner conviction and outward speech. This narration is foundational in Shia scholarship for understanding *ikhlas* (sincerity), emphasizing that true faith requires the tongue and heart to be unified, as duplicity creates a dissonance akin to two swords in one sheath. The reference to 'thoughts' (al-adhhan) further extends this principle to the cognitive realm, suggesting that mental focus must also align with verbal and emotional truth.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Abdul Rashman Bin Hammad, raising it, said,

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> blessed and High Said to Isa<sup>as</sup> Ibn Maryam<sup>as</sup>: “O Isa<sup>as</sup>! Let your<sup>as</sup> tongue during the privacy and the public be one tongue, and similar to that, your heart. I<sup>azwj</sup> Caution you<sup>as</sup> of yourself<sup>as</sup> and suffice with Me<sup>azwj</sup> as an All-Knowing.
It is not correct for there to be two tongues in one mouth, nor two swords in one sheath, nor two hearts in one chest, and similar to that are the minds’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Asbat from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn Hammad in a marfu’ manner from the Imam who has said the following:

“Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, said to Jesus, son of Mary (peace be upon them), ‘O Jesus, your tongue must be one tongue in private and in public so also must be your heart. I warn you against your own soul and Myself am a sufficient expert over your (activities).
Two tongues are not proper for one mouth just as two swords are not proper in one sheath or two hearts in one chest, and so also are minds.’”
